papers.title: CrossLiDAR: Controllable Multi-Sensor LiDAR Sequence Generation
papers.abstract: High-fidelity LiDAR simulation remains a bottleneck for scalable development and validation of autonomous systems. Existing generators can synthesize realistic scans, but they are typically constrained to a single sensor configuration, offer limited control over structure and geometry, and drift in long-horizon 4D generation. We present CrossLiDAR, a unified transformer-based framework capable of generating controllable and spatio-temporally consistent multi-sensor LiDAR sequences. Our approach leverages a rectified flow objective with a Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) backbone, within a compact latent space of range images. To support multiple LiDAR sensors, an Inter-sensor Module enables interaction across sensors, while a ControlNet-style branch provides structural conditioning (e.g., BEV priors or 3D bounding boxes). For modeling the temporal consistency, CrossLiDAR generates short $N$-frame sequences and extends them autoregressively to improve long-horizon coherence. Our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average improvement of 29.56\% in JSD and 15.36\% in MMD evaluated on nuScenes and the Waymo Dataset. CrossLiDAR bridges the gap to modern autonomous-driving simulation by enabling calibration-consistent multi-sensor LiDAR rollouts over long horizons for controllable, scenario-based testing.

papers.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

papers.title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables
papers.abstract: We present SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented framework for text-to-3D scene generation in which deformable objects, such as cloth, stuffed toys and ropes, are generated as physically valid, simulation-ready bodies and placed in intersection-free contact with the furniture that supports them, with one another and with themselves. Existing physics-augmented pipelines simulate rigid bodies only and cannot accommodate a generated deformable object, which text-to-3D generation returns as a geometrically invalid mesh, sometimes self-intersecting, that has no rest shape, no material model and no admissible initial state. These are the inputs a deformable simulation requires, and we construct each from information already in the pipeline. The rest shape comes from how the object is manufactured rather than from the generated physically inconsistent deformed configuration, and a material library assigns each deformable object its initial elastic parameters, which can then be optimized. The occluded support is regenerated and converted into a watertight collision mesh, each object is released from an optimizable placement above the supporting part that the prompt specifies, and the complete scene is driven to static equilibrium under one unified contact model, with completion verified by geometric checks and a vision-language model. When a scene fails the prompt, a grid search over placements corrects it, and the adjoint of a differentiable simulation of the same contact energy reaches the targets the grid does not, places several bodies jointly and recovers and optimizes material parameters. Multi-body scenes equilibrate in a single simulation, and the pipeline also runs from the text prompt alone. On all sixty-five prompts, SoftPAT3D produces no undesired interpenetration of any kind, whereas every other system does, and its scenes directly support scene editing and robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Internal Computation for Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Iterative neural policies usually spend the same computation on every decision, although the benefit of additional processing varies across states. We introduce Adaptive Internal Computation (AIC), an iterative policy that learns when to stop refining its latent representation and act. In AIC, we train action selection and stopping jointly, an expected-depth penalty values computation and intermediate value predictions provide auxiliary supervision. We show that when only some states benefit from further refinement, an ideal state-dependent allocator outperforms every state-independent stopping schedule at the same expected depth. With at most eight refinement steps per decision, AIC executes 3.3 steps on average across twelve benchmark tasks and lowers per-decision latency by 31--44% relative to a fixed eight-step policy on four control and robotics tasks. Its mean reward exceeds the best fixed-depth policy on seven tasks and trails it on four. Ablating adaptive stopping and value supervision separately shows that stopping accounts for most of the reward gain on PickCube and AntMaze, where it also executes more refinement steps and that supervision accounts for most of it on RareEvent.

papers.title: Locating and Repairing Domain Shift in VLM Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as end-to-end driving planners, yet they suffer from cross-city domain shift. Existing methods treat this shift as a single quantity addressed by uniform alignment or single-site editing. We challenge this view on two counts: (i) domain shift in VLM trajectory planners is inherently structured across modality and layer, and (ii) a locate-then-repair recipe matched to this structure outperforms every uniform-objective baseline. We analyse domain shift via activation patching and uncover two regularities. (F1) Modality axis. Image and text tokens exhibit distinct shift patterns in each VLM. (F2) Layer axis. The layer-wise shift partition is architecture-dependent and dataset-stable. These findings recast domain shift as a two-dimensional tensor indexed by modality (image vs. text tokens) and layer, motivating a simple principle: locate where shift occurs, and repair only there. We instantiate this principle in MoLaRx (Modality-Layer Repair), a locate-then-repair framework. The Causal Importance Score (CIS) estimates the domain shift as a modality-layer tensor and partitions the layers into functional zones. CIS-Guided Selective Repair (CISR) then applies a matched operator (Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) / low-rank adaptation (LoRA) / freezing) to repair each zone, with the composition adapting automatically to each architecture. We evaluate MoLaRx on three architecturally distinct VLMs (LFM2-VL-1.6B, Qwen2-VL-2B, and PaliGemma2-3B) across two cross-city benchmarks (nuScenes and Argoverse 2). MoLaRx attains the lowest cross-city trajectory-error gap among adaptation methods in all six main-table settings, while using 50-60% fewer trainable parameters and 8.4-10.9 ms lower inference latency. In contrast, uniform MMD-only adaptation collapses in all six settings, highlighting the importance of structure-guided repair.

papers.title: PLS-GS: Probabilistic Lidar Scaffolds for Compact, Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is typically optimized from images only, many robotics and mapping applications provide both camera and high-definition LiDAR data, combining rich visual appearance with accurate geometric structure. We introduce PLS-GS, a probabilistic LiDAR scaffold for Gaussian Splatting that exploits this complementary sensing setting to construct a compact 3DGS representation aligned to the measured surface. PLS-GS fits a Hierarchical Gaussian Mixture Model jointly over position and color, yielding a continuous and adaptive scaffold that eliminates the need for discrete scene partitioning such as voxel grids or octrees. The fitted mixture then guides the renderable 3DGS Gaussians: each rendering Gaussian is associated with a GMM component and constrained in the local surface frame induced by that component's covariance. A Mahalanobis support loss bounds the deviation of the rendering Gaussians from the corresponding LiDAR-derived surface. Across five large outdoor scenes, PLS-GS places primitives markedly closer to the LiDAR measurements than both image- and LiDAR-initialized baselines, while employing substantially fewer primitives, yielding a considerably more compact model and faster rendering. At matched capacity, PLS-GS places primitives closer to the LiDAR measurements, with comparable rendering quality. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.

papers.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
papers.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. Transient 3D thermal simulations show that this inefficiency is also a thermal one, since sustained back-to-back planning heats a millimeter-scale silicon tile to 556 K even behind an ideal copper heat spreader. Guided by this chain from bound to bottleneck, we propose the World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA), a chip architecture for embedded world model planning that combines near-memory computation, real-time entropy estimation, variable-precision rollout units, and copy-on-write latent scratchpads. With a design target of 40x lower power, the same tile stays near ambient at 306 K in simulation, pointing toward practical planning on thermally constrained robots.

papers.title: How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning
papers.abstract: Pretrained vision language action (VLA) models show strong zero-shot performance but they are rarely deployed directly and are often first post-trained on demonstrations from the target setting. Yet VLAs are typically compared by zero-shot or full-data fine-tuned success which reveals little about the data and compute required for downstream adaptation. We study adaptation efficiency for six VLAs ($\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, and GR00T N1-N1.7) on four LIBERO suites, varying both demonstrations and training steps. This reveals differences hidden by full-data fine-tuning: models which are within two points on the full LIBERO-Spatial dataset differ by up to 3$\times$ in success with 50 demonstrations. $\pi_{0.5}$ needs 2-5$\times$ fewer demonstrations than $\pi_0$ and is the most sample-efficient model at every budget, with the largest gap on the long-horizon suite. Within GR00T, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three of four suites, despite their stronger zero-shot performance. We also study one pretraining factor behind these differences by freezing the VLM during finetuning: this severely degrades the $\pi$ models whose VLM is jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, but barely affects GR00T models.

papers.title: Industry case studies of adapting TTS for smooth interactions
papers.abstract: Modern, neural-based ASR and TTS systems for speech communication are now very sophisticated, but they are frequently designed for average users in more idealized scenarios, which can underperform when interacting with users having specialized listening needs, or who speak in non-standard ways. Here we review recent TTS research, and note that industrial, production-level implementations of adaptive TTS systems are scarce. We describe how we implemented changes to TTS systems based on prior research, and then report qualitative results from two case studies, where adapted TTS techniques are applied to real-world HRI settings: First, in an older adult care home, and second, in an airport, where noise levels create comprehension problems. Results suggest promising directions using relatively simple modifications to pitch, duration, and intensity of the robot's speech, and offer a framework for larger, more formal studies of how TTS adaptations can improve HRI.

papers.title: Engagement Estimation in Human-Robot and Human-Human Interactions across Domain, Age and Culture: MultiMediate'26 Challenge
papers.abstract: Understanding engagement in human interaction is essential for modelling assistive and context-aware AI systems. Previously, the MultiMediate challenge has focused on estimating momentary continuous engagement values in adult conversation across cultures, achieving high levels of generalisability across domains. However, engagement can be measured in different metrics and manifest differently between children and adults. MultiMediate'26 therefore expands the evaluated domain set to include the PInSoRo dataset of Child-Child and Child-Robot play sessions in English. These sessions were annotated categorically with task and social engagement, diversifying engagement types, age ranges and interaction types. In this paper, we describe the MultiMediate'26 challenge and its goals, introduce the NoXi, NoXi-J, MPIIGI, and PInSoRo datasets, showcase extracted multi-modal features, present our baseline model for engagement estimation across all domains, and discuss challenge submissions and approaches. In an effort to provide a transparent and welcoming challenge environment, baseline code, leaderboard, datasets, and extracted features are publicly available at this https URL .

papers.title: How to start a conversation proactively?
papers.abstract: Proactively initiating a conversation is a fundamental social competence and a critical capability for social robots. However, determining how and when to start a conversation in a given situation remains an open challenge, primarily due to the lack of a principled definition of conversational context. While recent large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive conversational fluency, they are predominantly turn-reactive and often produce generic or monotonous openers when tasked with initiating interaction, even when contextual information is available. Such limitations are particularly problematic for embodied social robots, where inappropriate or poorly timed initiations can negatively affect user engagement and rapport. In this work, we propose a schema of contextual variables that jointly characterize situations relevant for proactive conversation initiation. The schema is designed to structure perceptual, situational, and interactional cues such that they can be effectively exploited by language models. Furthermore, motivated by the absence of suitable training data, we introduce a curated dataset of contextually-aligned conversation openers (CCO) covering diverse everyday scenarios. Using this dataset, we fine-tune small language models (SLMs) to generate proactive conversation initiations. Through a comparative evaluation involving zero-shot LLMs, off-the-shelf SLMs, and our fine-tuned models, we demonstrate that explicit contextual structuring and targeted data curation substantially improve the quality and contextual appropriateness of conversation openers. Our results highlight the importance of context modeling for proactive social interaction and provide actionable building blocks for conversational robots.

papers.title: Building Rapport with Self-Disclosure in Human-Robot Interaction
papers.abstract: As social robots become increasingly present in everyday environments, establishing rapport with users is critical for enabling sustained and meaningful human-robot interaction. In human-human communication, self-disclosure is a well-established mechanism for building rapport; however, its role and impact in human-robot interaction (HRI) are not yet well understood. Although recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have improved the linguistic competence of conversational robots, such systems are typically deployed as reactive information providers, offering limited social reciprocity and relational depth. In this article, we investigate the role of robot self-disclosure in fostering rapport during face-to-face human-robot interaction. We propose a dialogue system, called RADIA that leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to enable a robot to retrieve and reference simulated autobiographical memories, allowing first-person self-disclosure to be incorporated naturally into ongoing conversations. We evaluate the proposed approach through an in-person user study, comparing interactions with a self-disclosing robot against a baseline non-self-disclosing robot. Our results show that robot self-disclosure significantly influences conversational dynamics and enhances users' perceived rapport with the robot, suggesting that self-disclosure is a valuable social behavior for long-term and socially engaging human-robot interaction.

papers.title: KR A1: Design and Preliminary Evaluation of a Humanoid-Robot Interaction Prototype Integrating Personalized Voice Synthesis, Contextual Dialogue, and Emotion-Aware Response Generation
papers.abstract: This paper presents the design and preliminary evaluation of KR A1, a humanoid-robot interaction prototype that integrates personalized voice synthesis, contextual dialogue processing, and emotion-aware response generation for potential mental-healthcare applications. The system architecture combines a locally hosted large language model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, served via Ollama) for natural-language understanding and response generation, OpenVoice v2 for zero-shot speaker-adaptive speech synthesis, and a two-tier emotion-processing pipeline comprising a keyword heuristic and LLM-based inference. Face recognition (InsightFace) and vector memory retrieval (FAISS with sentence-transformer embeddings) enable user-personalized interaction. The experimental evaluation reported here is limited to the voice-cloning component: cloned voices were evaluated against reference recordings using eight acoustic similarity measures - mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, pitch, spectral centroid, spectral contrast, spectral rolloff, zero-crossing rate, formants, and speaker-embedding cosine similarity - supplemented by a same-speaker versus cross-speaker baseline comparison. All tests were conducted on a small, informal development sample; no statistical significance testing against a held-out baseline was performed. The emotion-recognition accuracy, end-to-end response latency, and therapeutic or clinical impact of the integrated system have not yet been formally evaluated and are identified as directions for future work. All testing was informal and self-conducted by the development team; no patients or external human participants were involved, and the system has not been evaluated or deployed in a clinical setting.

executive_summary: Several works advance robust and risk-aware control and navigation: BRACE uses hierarchical RL with disturbance beliefs for reach-avoid under unknown spatially varying disturbances, improving performance over MPC and RL baselines in simulated quadcopter wind fields and on Crazyflie hardware; a capturability-aware sequential MPC for Linear Inverted Pendulum humanoids plans footsteps via safe-corridor rectangles with recursive feasibility and handles unexpected clutter (e.g., closed doors) in high-fidelity Digit simulations; SmoothedTurboMPC combines SQP with a log-barrier-smoothed ADMM inner loop to yield GPU-parallel differentiable MPC whose coupling with SHAC boosts training throughput up to 4.4× versus differentiable MPC baselines and achieves higher-return, 46× faster vehicle-racing training and successful full-scale race-car transfer; an SMC-based view of sampling MPC unifies many planners (MPPI, CEM, etc.) and shows that resampling cuts collision rates in long-horizon navigation and, with programmable proposals, raises push-T success from 1% to 100% in simulation and 10% to 90% on a Franka FR3; and a transformer policy that imitates LQG delivers median closed-loop cost within 0.4% of optimal on seen LTI systems and within 1.0% after light fine-tuning on unseen ones without explicit plant models or state estimators at run time.

New frameworks improve dexterous, bimanual, and humanoid manipulation: GUARD Q-steers generative robot policies using anomaly-informed value functions to boost Adroit dexterous manipulation success to 96.0% nominal and 80.0% perturbed in simulation and add 40 and 25 percentage points in sim-to-real screwdriver tasks; object-centric bimanual RL with shared rewards yields emergent skills such as pre-grasping, regrasping, and handover, and a DAgger/RL-distilled policy achieves 76.3% success over four real tasks and 85.0% simulated barcode-scanning success versus 60.4% for two single-arm policies; BetaGrasp adds a grasp-taxonomy label to a 3D diffusion DP3 point-cloud policy, raising correct grasp-type rate from 25% to 94% in simulation and, on hardware climbing-hold trials, increasing mean slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N while cutting fully slipping grasps from 44% to 10%; and DexForesight injects representations from an action-conditioned spatial world model into dexterous policies, improving DexJoCo success from 49.4% to 60.5% and raising real-robot dexterous task success from 50.0% to 58.3%.

Several systems target cross-embodiment learning, motion understanding, and coding-based robot control: UniLatent aligns source and target visual encoders via simulated paired renderings to enable cross-embodiment policy transfer, reaching up to 93% zero-shot success and beating pixel-level baselines by >30 percentage points, and in xArm-to-Franka transfer attains 27/30 successful fine-tuned rollouts using only 10 target demos per task; a unified inertial encoder with kinematic IMU synthesis jointly trains on human and retargeted humanoid motion to produce a shared inertial interface, achieving the lowest velocity error (including 0.099 m/s on a real Unitree G1) and supporting motion–description retrieval for motions only seen in human data; BATCH learns behavior-aligned temporal representations and a video-action diffusion policy with cycle-consistent human–robot alignment and style transfer, improving real-world manipulation generalization over unaligned and prior cross-embodiment baselines; a self-learning coding agent pipeline progressively acquires bimanual object-flipping skills in simulation, boosting success from 24.7% to 95.0% and encoding strategies into graph-based control code that transfers to physical robots; and the Embodied First Exam provides 1,156 coding-agent control tasks on 47 robots with three evaluation settings, where the strongest evaluated agent reaches 34% success on 456 core tasks, indicating large headroom and enabling detailed failure-stage analysis.

Vision-language-action and multi-domain decision-making are advanced by new architectures and distillation schemes: DASH decouples a slow vision-language backbone from a fast flow-matching action head into asynchronous System 2/System 1 processes, maintaining 20 Hz control for 0.8B–8B backbones where synchronous pipelines fall to 4.1 Hz, and achieving higher RoboTwin benchmark success and better real-humanoid pick-and-place performance; DreamVLA converts generated human motion trajectories into RL-trained task trajectories and uses reference-conditioned DAgger restarts to mitigate distribution shift, training VLAs on humanoid tasks like platform picking, drawer opening, and button pressing; DeltaForge consolidates N per-domain autonomous-driving VLA experts into a post-hoc mixture-of-experts that SVD-decomposes weight deltas into shared and tiny domain-specific components with lightweight routers, matching per-domain experts and outperforming merging, routing, centralized, and federated baselines across six driving domains while enabling cheap addition of new domains and generalization to unseen domain combinations; and Kinematic Action Models treat whole-body motion generation (via the Kimodo backbone plus ControlNet conditioning and root–body–hand hierarchy) as the core loco-manipulation action, with Kimodo-Policy reaching 72.14% success on HumanoidArena, competitive SIMPLE results, and 60% mean success on eight real tasks using a 678M-parameter model with 92M trainable parameters.

Multiple works improve modeling, simulation, and representation learning for complex dynamics and deformable or soft systems: an extended aSSM framework learns a 5D reduced ODE directly on a soft-helicoid trunk robot and embeds it in MPC to achieve higher-accuracy real-time tracking across 2D/3D tasks than linear and model-free RL baselines; a complementary study uses a 6D aSSM-reduced model as a sample-efficient RL training environment for a pneumatic soft arm, allowing 3 hours of simulator training (vs. an estimated 3 years on hardware) and yielding 40% lower hardware tracking error than policies trained on much larger RNN and transformer surrogates whose identification requires 13 and 100 hours; DeepSoMo enforces self-supervised latent prediction for proprioceptive deformable motion estimation and, against FEM ground truth, consistently improves global trajectory, orientation, shape, and contact inference over recurrent baselines; SoftPAT3D turns text prompts into physics-consistent 3D scenes with deformable objects by generating rest shapes, material models, watertight supports, and using grid search plus adjoint-based differentiable simulation to fix prompt failures and jointly optimize placements and materials, producing 65 prompted scenes without unwanted interpenetrations; and a differentiable-simulation taxonomy clarifies gradient referents and adjoint realizations, introduces an orthogonal contact-handling taxonomy and four quantified gradient-degradation mechanisms, and provides a diagnostic tool, checklist, and research agenda outlining when exact derivatives, adjoints, or even zeroth-order methods are preferable.

New analyses, data-collection schemes, and benchmarks refine learning, perception, and navigation strategies: a study of VLA adaptation on LIBERO shows π₀.₅ needs roughly 2–5× fewer demonstrations than π₀ and is most sample-efficient at all data budgets, GR00T N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6/N1.7 on most suites despite weaker zero-shot performance, and freezing vision-language modules affects π and GR00T families differently; vine sampling for behavior cloning augments selected states with k demonstrations from the same observation, enabling diffusion policies to better capture multi-modal action distributions and improving proximity to demonstrators and best-of-N and expert-iteration performance on a 2D truck-unloading task; a controlled peeling benchmark shows that coordinate frames and information content critically shape learned predictive models—surface-relative coordinates aid consequence prediction and counterfactual selection but remain sensitive to coordinate uncertainty and contact/execution errors; a preference-augmented distributional RL navigation method encodes risk preferences as shifted quantile weights and, by optimizing for worst-case preference distributions, reduces collisions while improving task success over scalar CVaR-based approaches across simulated and real/simulated vehicles; CPNav calibrates VLM action scores via conformal prediction for map-free object-goal navigation, yielding SR/SPL gains of 6.2/11.4% on HM3D and 12.4/8.8% on MP3D, and 24.9/15.2% on a real robot over uncalibrated baselines; monocular model-based imitation learning with a learned collision-risk model and demonstration-tuned optimization parameters reduces collision rates and improves reliability across different robots versus end-to-end imitation and classic model-based baselines; DeepSoMo-based work (separate from the taxonomy) and BAT-WAM demonstrate improved tactile and deformable sensing—BAT-WAM’s RGB-conditioned tactile/action codebooks cut tactile RMSE by up to ~39% versus HandTouch and slash future tactile-prediction RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM; MOSU2 adds contextual reasoning plus conditional retrieval of geometric/dynamic evidence for outdoor navigation, raising real-world mean success from 61.8% to 94.2% and condition-detection accuracy from 72.2% to 91.4%; FLAVOR’s hierarchical spatio-temporal mapping for UAV exploration compresses global information into keyframes and topological graphs, cutting exploration time by ~32–42% and map memory by 94–99% in simulation and by 62–93% in real deployments; stochastic challenges are proposed as a benchmark paradigm using reproducible yet varied real scenes, with a mobile-manipulation benchmark and cross-lab robot comparison illustrating platform-agnostic evaluation; a study of teleoperator demonstration quality defines a ‘data multiple’ and finds that on robomimic’s Square task, Worse operators need 1.55× more demos at a 25 s time limit (shrinking to 1.11× at 100 s), mixed-quality datasets underperform a linear-value model, and Worse operators are only cost-effective if their wage is under one-third of Better operators given longer demo times; a particle-filter wrapper around a single diffusion model that jointly represents states, actions, and observations maintains multiple state histories and reweights them by observational likelihood, improving state estimation and task performance versus direct model action generation in simulated partially observed navigation and manipulation; and a hybrid tendon–linkage robotic finger with four mechanical DOFs and three actuators demonstrates contact-dependent adaptive grasping without an actively driven DIP joint and achieves a mean peak fingertip force of 4.56 N across diverse object shapes.

institution_matches.title: GUARD: Anomaly-Informed Q-Steering for Generative Robot Policies in Dexterous Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes GUARD, an anomaly-informed Q-steering framework that combines sparse task rewards with dense anomaly scores learned from the policy’s training data, using a learned Q-function to steer the denoising process of generative robot policies without modifying the pretrained policy. In simulation on four Adroit dexterous manipulation tasks, GUARD achieves average success rates of 96.0% under nominal dynamics and 80.0% under perturbed dynamics, outperforming the strongest baseline by 21.0 and 20.0 percentage points respectively while maintaining the lowest anomaly scores. In sim-to-real experiments on in-hand screwdriver rotation and reorientation tasks, GUARD transfers directly to hardware, improving success rates by 40 and 25 percentage points compared to baselines.
claims: The paper proposes GUARD, an anomaly-informed Q-steering framework that combines sparse task rewards with dense anomaly scores learned from the policy’s training data, using a learned Q-function to steer the denoising process of generative robot policies without modifying the pretrained policy.

In simulation on four Adroit dexterous manipulation tasks, GUARD achieves average success rates of 96.0% under nominal dynamics and 80.0% under perturbed dynamics, outperforming the strongest baseline by 21.0 and 20.0 percentage points respectively while maintaining the lowest anomaly scores.
In sim-to-real experiments on in-hand screwdriver rotation and reorientation tasks, GUARD transfers directly to hardware, improving success rates by 40 and 25 percentage points compared to baselines.

institution_matches.title: SimDuoReal: Object-Centric Bimanual Policy for Emergent Dexterity
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Stanford University; UC San Diego
institution_matches.overview: The paper trains bimanual reinforcement learning policies with a shared object-centric reward across varied environments, leading to emergent behaviors such as pre-grasp manipulation, grasping, regrasping, in-hand adjustment, and handover without hand-designed motion sequences. Expert policies are refined on transition states and distilled via DAgger and reinforcement learning into a single bimanual policy that composes the learned behaviors for diverse tasks. On real hardware, the distilled policy achieves 76.3% success (61/80 trials) across four tasks with unseen objects and no task-specific fine-tuning, and in simulated barcode scanning it attains 85.0% success versus 60.4% for two single-arm policies without handover.
claims: The paper trains bimanual reinforcement learning policies with a shared object-centric reward across varied environments, leading to emergent behaviors such as pre-grasp manipulation, grasping, regrasping, in-hand adjustment, and handover without hand-designed motion sequences.
Expert policies are refined on transition states and distilled via DAgger and reinforcement learning into a single bimanual policy that composes the learned behaviors for diverse tasks.

On real hardware, the distilled policy achieves 76.3% success (61/80 trials) across four tasks with unseen objects and no task-specific fine-tuning, and in simulated barcode scanning it attains 85.0% success versus 60.4% for two single-arm policies without handover.

institution_matches.title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
institution_matches.institution: ETH Zurich; Massachusetts Institute of Technology
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces BRACE, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances that infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and conditions a high-level policy combining nominal and belief-guided residual terms, trained with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. In three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields and on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance compared to model predictive control and reinforcement learning baselines.
claims: The paper introduces BRACE, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances that infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and conditions a high-level policy combining nominal and belief-guided residual terms, trained with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic.

In three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields and on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance compared to model predictive control and reinforcement learning baselines.

institution_matches.title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that splits a vision-language-action policy into a slow vision-language backbone (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) running as concurrent processes, so that control rate is determined by the action head and becomes independent of backbone size. DASH’s action head fuses stale semantics from the frozen backbone with fresh visual inputs from its own ResNet encoder, is trained under desynchronized conditions to handle observation staleness, and uses an adaptive temporal aggregator to align overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On the asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark, DASH maintains a 20 Hz control rate for backbone sizes from 0.8B to 8B parameters while a synchronous pipeline drops from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, achieving higher success at every size; on a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH yields clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

institution_matches.title: Grasp-Taxonomy Conditioning as a Mode Switch for Dexterous Grasping of Climbing Holds
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces BetaGrasp, a 3D diffusion-based DP3-style point-cloud grasping policy for a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand, conditioned on a four-class grasp taxonomy label (crimp, sloper, pinch, jug) to act as a discrete mode switch for dexterous grasping of climbing holds. Analysis shows the point-cloud encoder alone does not separate the four hold types, and a label-free DP3-style baseline collapses to jug grasps from the reset pose, achieving 25% correct grasp type versus 94% for BetaGrasp in simulated rollouts. On 80 paired hardware trials on a climbing-hold benchmark with a slip-force ratchet testbed, BetaGrasp increases average slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N and reduces fully slipping grasps from 44% of trials to 10%.

institution_matches.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes stochastic challenges as a new paradigm for real-world robot manipulation benchmarking, using reproducible but stochastically varied real-world scenes to mimic the rigor and surprise of hidden test sets while enabling system-level innovation and cross-platform comparability via success rates over shared task distributions. A concrete stochastic benchmark for mobile manipulation is implemented, and two robots tested in two different labs are compared on this benchmark to demonstrate how performance across different platforms and locations can be evaluated under the proposed paradigm.

institution_matches.title: Capturability-Aware Footstep Planning in Cluttered Environments: A Recursively Feasible Sequential MPC on Axis-Aligned Safe Corridors
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents a capturability-aware sequential Model Predictive Control framework for Linear Inverted Pendulum humanoid footstep planning in cluttered environments, combining obstacle avoidance with capturability constraints using axis-aligned safe corridors formed by sequences of intersecting rectangles, and providing recursive feasibility guarantees for the planning layer. The planner can autonomously adapt to constrained scenarios, including switching to in-place walking when forward motion is blocked by unexpected obstructions such as doors assumed open during planning but closed during execution, and its performance remains largely independent of prediction horizon, enabling high success rates at low computational cost. The approach is validated in high-fidelity simulations with the humanoid robot Digit, demonstrating practical capturable footstep planning in cluttered environments.

institution_matches.title: DreamVLA: From Generated Human Motions to Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Policies
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes DreamVLA, a method that uses generated human motion trajectories to guide reinforcement learning in simulation, converting them into reliable task execution trajectories that can train vision-language-action models without additional task-specific teleoperation data. A central component is a reference-conditioned DAgger distillation procedure that, after failed learner rollouts, restarts the RL expert from sampled learner states with the same reference suffix and aggregates successful corrective trajectories, mitigating distribution shift left by offline imitation. DreamVLA is evaluated on humanoid tasks including picking from a platform, opening a drawer, pressing a button, and walking and picking from a platform, with ablations over DAgger iterations, residual reinforcement learning, and the scale of the generated dataset.

institution_matches.title: DeltaForge: A Post-hoc Mixture-of-Experts VLA for Multi-Domain Autonomous Driving
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces DeltaForge, a post-hoc mixture-of-experts vision-language-action model for multi-domain autonomous driving that consolidates N independently fine-tuned per-domain experts into a single model using only their weights and a small proxy dataset. DeltaForge jointly decomposes all per-domain weight updates via singular value decomposition into a shared component and tiny domain-specific components, and trains two clip-level blind routers (for VLM reasoning and flow-matching dynamics) that route only the small domain-specific pieces based on soft labels from the proxy dataset, keeping routing efficient. Across six diverse driving domains, DeltaForge approaches the per-domain experts’ accuracy and surpasses merging, routing, centralized, and federated baselines at near single-model parameter and compute cost, while allowing new domains to be added by projecting their weight updates onto the shared basis without end-to-end retraining and enabling generalization to unseen domain combinations.

institution_matches.title: Embodied First Exam
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Stanford University; UC Berkeley; University of Washington
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces the Embodied First Exam, a unified and agent-native evaluation framework for coding agents controlling robots, comprising 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites covering spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. The benchmark defines three evaluation settings: a Standard Setting with only sensor observations and no default environment resets, a Realtime variant where the environment continues running while the agent reasons, and a Privileged Setting with full simulator state and unlimited resets for searching oracle solutions and establishing approximate upper bounds. On 456 core tasks in the Embodied First Exam, the strongest of eight evaluated agents, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, achieves a 34% success rate in the Standard Setting, indicating substantial remaining headroom for improvement; failure analysis categorizes the stages at which attempts break down across agents, settings, and stage categories.

institution_matches.title: Efficient Learning of Differentiable MPC Policies on the GPU via Smoothed ADMM and First-Order Reinforcement Learning
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes SmoothedTurboMPC, a GPU-parallel differentiable MPC solver that combines SQP with a log-barrier-smoothed ADMM inner loop to obtain smooth gradients, exact sensitivities at convergence, and efficient batched policy evaluation. Coupling SmoothedTurboMPC with first-order reinforcement learning via SHAC, which reuses rollout MPC solutions, yields up to 4.4× higher end-to-end training throughput than state-of-the-art differentiable MPC baselines in simulation experiments. On a vehicle racing task, the proposed framework achieves higher returns than an MPC PPO approach with a 46× speedup, training on 3.3 million transitions in 7 minutes, and is further used with domain randomization to train a more reliable MPC racing policy validated on a full-scale race car.

institution_matches.title: UniLatent: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Latent Observation Alignment
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces UniLatent, a cross-embodiment transfer framework that renders paired source–target robot observations in simulation and aligns a source visual encoder to a frozen target encoder so that a policy trained on source demonstrations can run directly on target observations in a shared latent space. Across three simulation tasks and two target robot arms, UniLatent achieves up to 93% zero-shot success and exceeds the strongest pixel-level image translation baseline by over 30 percentage points on average. In real-world xArm-to-Franka transfer, UniLatent enables fine-tuning with only 10 target demonstrations per task to reach 27 successful rollouts out of 30.

institution_matches.title: A Unified Inertial Encoder for Human and Humanoid Motion
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Stanford University; UC Berkeley
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes a unified inertial encoder that uses kinematic IMU synthesis to represent human and humanoid motion at corresponding body sites, enabling joint training on human and retargeted humanoid motion for velocity estimation and motion–text alignment under a shared inertial interface. With continuous-time encoding and sensor and motion randomization, the resulting model transfers zero-shot to a physical Unitree G1 without physics simulation, real-robot training trajectories, or fine-tuning, and achieves the lowest velocity error among evaluated methods on five datasets, including 0.099 m/s on real G1. The unified encoder supports motion–description retrieval for retargeted G1 motion categories observed only in human training data, indicating that human motion knowledge can improve generalization in humanoid inertial odometry and language-grounded motion understanding.

institution_matches.title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents a self-learning pipeline in which a coding agent autonomously develops and refines object-flipping strategies for a bimanual robot through iterative learning in physics simulation across diverse object geometries, progressing from simple handover to toppling, pushing, robust grasping, sensing, and thin-object manipulation with recovery. Progressive skill acquisition in simulation increases flipping task success from 24.7% to 95.0%. The learned skills are encoded in a graph-based control code that combines high-level strategy selection with reactive control, enabling multi-stage flipping on physical robots.

institution_matches.title: How Many Demonstrations Does a VLA Need? On the Sample Efficiency of VLA Finetuning
institution_matches.overview: The paper empirically studies adaptation efficiency of six pretrained vision-language-action models (π₀, π₀.₅, and GR00T N1–N1.7) on four LIBERO suites by varying both the number of demonstrations and training steps, revealing large differences in performance under limited data that are not evident under full-data fine-tuning. Model π₀.₅ requires approximately 2–5× fewer demonstrations than π₀ and is the most sample-efficient model at every data budget, with the largest advantage on a long-horizon suite; within GR00T models, N1.5 adapts more efficiently than N1.6 and N1.7 on three out of four suites despite their stronger zero-shot performance. Freezing the vision-language module during finetuning substantially degrades the π models, whose VLM was jointly trained with the action expert during pretraining, while having minimal effect on GR00T models, indicating differing pretraining dependencies.

institution_matches.title: BATCH: Behavior Alignment for Cross-Embodiment Learning from Humans
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces BATCH, a cross-embodiment learning framework that learns self-supervised temporal representations with a cycle-consistency objective to align human and robot behaviors without manual annotation, and incorporates these correspondences into an autoregressive video-action diffusion model. BATCH employs two training objectives—behavior-aligned co-training and human-to-robot style transfer—to exploit cross-embodiment correspondences when learning robot policies from human demonstrations. On real-world manipulation tasks, BATCH improves generalization to unseen task configurations compared to training on unaligned data and prior cross-embodiment baselines, with additional performance gains from the style-transfer objective.

institution_matches.title: Action Representation for Spatial Generalization in Robot World Models
institution_matches.overview: The study systematically compares matched action representations defined in world, object, and surface coordinate frames on a controlled robotic peeling benchmark to analyze how spatial descriptions influence learned predictive models and spatial generalization. Experiments with global pose and contact relocation show that limited training data incurs a cost when equivalent interactions receive different spatial descriptions, and removing peel thickness information yields an irreducible ambiguity where identical inputs correspond to different material removal outcomes. Action coordinates defined relative to the surface enable better consequence prediction and counterfactual action selection under accurate local observations, but learned predictors remain vulnerable to uncertainty in the coordinate frame; joint centering of surface and tool removes sensitivity to origin translation while incorrect contact geometry and execution deviations introduce distinct failure modes, illustrating that preserving action–state physical relationships is key for spatial generalization.

institution_matches.title: Explicitly capturing demonstrator multi-modality for distillation into diffusion policies
institution_matches.overview: The paper adapts vine sampling to behavior cloning data collection by querying a demonstrator k times from exactly the same observation at selected states, explicitly capturing multi-modal conditional action distributions that standard sliding-window collection does not disambiguate. On a synthetic task, increasing the number of actions per observation k leads diffusion policies to more accurately match the demonstrator’s conditional distribution, including its multi-modality and diversity, instead of memorizing a single action per observation. On a 2D truck unloading task, vine sampling produces policies that are closer to the demonstrator and substantially improves both best-of-N performance and expert-iteration performance compared to standard data collection.

institution_matches.title: SoftPAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation with Deformables
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents SoftPAT3D, a physics-augmented text-to-3D scene generation framework that converts generated deformable objects (e.g., cloth, stuffed toys, ropes) into simulation-ready bodies with rest shapes, material models from a library, and admissible initial states, and then drives the full scene to static equilibrium under a unified contact model. SoftPAT3D regenerates occluded support geometry into watertight collision meshes, releases deformable objects from optimizable placements above specified supports, and uses grid search plus differentiable simulation adjoints to correct prompt failures, jointly place multiple bodies, and recover or optimize material parameters. Across 65 text prompts, SoftPAT3D produces scenes without undesired interpenetrations, unlike all compared systems, and its outputs are directly usable for scene editing and robotic manipulation.

institution_matches.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes using particle filtering with a single pretrained generative diffusion model that jointly represents states, actions, and observations, maintaining multiple state-history hypotheses whose predicted observations and action proposals are generated by the model and reweighted by agreement with incoming measurements. Unlike conventional use of particle filtering solely for state estimation, the approach also guides action selection by favoring proposals associated with higher-weight particles that better explain the observations. Simulation experiments on partially observed navigation and vision-based manipulation tasks show that this particle-filter-based inference improves both state estimation quality and task performance compared to directly using the same pretrained model for action generation without filtering.

institution_matches.title: The Relative Value of Demonstration Data: Execution Time Limits and Operator Mixtures in Behavior Cloning
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes measuring the relative value of robot teleoperator demonstration data via a 'data multiple': the ratio of demonstration counts two operator groups require for behavior cloning policies to reach the same success rate under a given execution time limit. On robomimic’s simulated Square task, within the 25-second time limit, policies trained on all-Worse demonstrations require 1.55× as many demonstrations as those trained on all-Better demonstrations, but this gap shrinks to a 1.11× multiple with a 100-second limit, indicating that much of the difference is due to later task completion rather than outright failure. On the Square task, mixtures of Better and Worse demonstrations perform worse than a simple linear value model would predict (e.g., a 50/50 mix needs 13% more demonstrations than implied by each Worse demo being worth 1/1.55 of a Better demo), this excess persists across 20–200 s time limits and under uniform-length sampling, and under a 25-second limit switching to Worse teleoperators is cost-effective only if their hourly wage is less than one-third that of Better teleoperators due to longer recording times.

institution_matches.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
institution_matches.overview: The paper extends an adiabatic spectral submanifold (aSSM)-based, purely data-driven modeling framework to hardware by learning a five-dimensional aSSM-reduced nonlinear ODE directly from data collected on a soft-helicoid trunk robot. Using the learned 5D aSSM-reduced ODE within a model predictive control scheme, the method achieves real-time precision closed-loop trajectory tracking for a variety of 2D and 3D tasks with static and dynamic constraints on the soft-helicoid trunk robot. Across all evaluated control tasks on the hardware platform, the aSSM-based methodology yields higher accuracy and precision than available data-driven linear models and model-free reinforcement learning baselines.

institution_matches.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes using an adiabatic spectral submanifold (aSSM)-reduced, low-dimensional polynomial ODE model, learned purely from pre-collected data, as a sample-efficient reinforcement learning training environment for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. On a pneumatically actuated soft arm, a trajectory-tracking policy trained for 3 hours on a six-dimensional aSSM-reduced model can be deployed on hardware without fine-tuning, whereas reproducing the same training directly on the robot would extrapolate to about 3 years of interaction time. institution_matches.title: DeepSoMo: Deformable Object Motion Estimation under Proprioceptive Partial Observability via Predictive Latent Dynamics
institution_matches.overview: The paper introduces DeepSoMo, a learning-based framework for deformable object motion estimation under proprioceptive partial observability that enforces predictive latent dynamics via a self-supervised latent prediction constraint to promote long-horizon latent temporal consistency. DeepSoMo is evaluated in a canonical deformable dynamics setting using high-fidelity finite-element simulation as ground truth, targeting estimation of global motion, orientation, shape evolution, and contact from internal sensing. Across these simulated deformable-body tasks, DeepSoMo consistently improves trajectory estimation, orientation recovery, shape reconstruction, and contact inference compared to architecture-matched recurrent baseline models.

institution_matches.title: Generalizable Output Feedback Optimal Control via Transformers Without Explicit State Estimation
institution_matches.overview: The paper proposes a transformer-based policy that learns generalizable output-feedback optimal control for a heterogeneous family of partially observed, noisy MIMO LTI systems by imitating LQG controllers, using standardized, padded, and masked representations augmented with encodings of cost and noise covariances, without explicit access to plant matrices or a state estimator at run time. The authors characterize how an optimal LQG controller, expressed as a dynamic state-space model, relates to a static transformer that acts on a finite window of noisy measurements, and they express the excess closed-loop cost of any causal policy as the energy of its deviation from the optimal LQG action. On 28 simulated systems, the trained transformer policy attains a median cost within 0.4% of optimal LQG for seen systems, and for unseen systems a light fine-tuning step yields a median cost gap of 1.0% relative to optimal.

institution_matches.title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Stanford University
institution_matches.overview: The paper presents a taxonomy for differentiable physics simulation that separates two axes: the referent of the returned derivative (finite computation, converged equation, or continuous dynamics) and the realization of the backward pass (automatic differentiation, equation-level adjoint solve, or custom adjoint), clarifying that the perceived trade-off between gradient exactness and memory stems from implementation choices rather than fundamental constraints. An orthogonal taxonomy is developed for handling contact in differentiable simulation, and four mechanisms by which useful gradients can be degraded are identified and empirically measured on a common testbed, showing that the benefit of exact derivatives over equation-level adjoints depends on both the fitting target and solver budget. The survey reviews model classes, systems techniques, and applications of differentiable simulation through this lens, and introduces a reporting checklist, an accompanying diagnostic tool that computes it, and a research agenda aimed at improving the use and evaluation of simulator gradients, including recognizing regimes where zeroth-order methods can outperform gradient-based approaches.

topic_matches.title: Preference-Augmented Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Sensitive Navigation
topic_matches.institution: Jilin University; The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces a preference-augmented distributional reinforcement learning approach for navigation that represents risk preferences as shifts in quantile-weight distributions within an Implicit Quantile Network framework, rather than relying on a single scalar Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) level. During training, the method exposes the agent to diverse risk preferences via preference-guided exploration, and at deployment it optimizes against the worst-case preference distribution to produce a conservative navigation policy that accounts for multiple risk profiles without heavy hyperparameter tuning or strong dependence on sensor signals under partial observability. Across simulated environments and real or simulated vehicle platforms, the proposed method reduces collisions while simultaneously improving task success compared to existing risk-sensitive navigation approaches based on scalar CVaR formulations.

topic_matches.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes CPNav, a map-free object-goal navigation framework that couples collision-aware motion primitive planning from RGB-D-derived navigability maps with statistically calibrated vision-language model (VLM) action scores obtained via conformal prediction using oracle actions from a tree-structured exploration with backtracking. CPNav’s conformal prediction layer calibrates scores from two VLMs for goal detection and action scoring, is model-agnostic, and provides finite-sample guarantees at a user-specified risk level; online, calibrated scores guide action selection while a stored exploration tree supports backtracking to alternative actions. In AI Habitat simulation, CPNav improves success rate (SR) and SPL relative to an uncalibrated VLM baseline by 6.2% and 11.4% on HM3D v0.2, and by 12.4% and 8.8% on MP3D; on a real Hiwonder MentorPi robot, CPNav yields SR and SPL gains of 24.9% and 15.2%, respectively.

topic_matches.title: Model-Based Imitation Learning For Monocular Vision-Based Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents a model-based imitation learning framework for monocular vision-based navigation in cluttered environments, where a learned collision model maps sequences of past images and candidate control sequences to a predictive distribution over worst-case obstacle clearance, which is then used to define a collision-risk cost in trajectory optimization. Human demonstrations are used to learn how to balance this collision-risk cost with other task-related costs such as goal progress, and also to learn algorithmic parameters of the optimizer (including warm starts) to accelerate the solution process. Across robots with different embodiments operating in cluttered environments, the proposed approach achieves highly reliable navigation and substantially reduces collision rates compared to recent end-to-end imitation learning and traditional model-based baselines.

topic_matches.title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference
topic_matches.overview: The paper shows that a broad family of sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) methods—including predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants—can all be expressed as a single Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference algorithm, parameterized by the choice of proposal distribution, update rule for aggregating cost-weighted particles into a nominal plan, and an effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. Evaluated on MuJoCo nonlinear control, open-loop obstacle-field navigation, 7-DoF motion planning, and non-prehensile push-T tasks in simulation and on a Franka FR3, the SMC-based planner uses resampling to mitigate particle degeneracy at long horizons, reducing collision rates by 30% at a 28-step horizon in the navigation domain relative to non-resampling baselines. By designing programmable proposal distributions within the SMC framework, the method improves push-T performance from 1% to 100% success in simulation and from 10% to 90% on hardware compared to perturbative sampling baselines.

topic_matches.title: BAT-WAM: Bridging Action and Touch in World-Action Models for Dexterous Hands
topic_matches.institution: Fudan University; Rimbot; Southeast University; Tsinghua University
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes BAT-WAM, a world-action modeling framework that learns separate tactile and action codebooks connected by an RGB-conditioned continuous latent bridge to jointly model visual context, hand joint state, and tactile information for dexterous hands. On HTBench, BAT-WAM reduces tactile reconstruction RMSE by 34.73% under fully masked and 38.84% under partially masked tactile conditions compared to an image-conditioned HandTouch baseline. For future tactile prediction using target-time RGB and historical actions, BAT-WAM reduces mean RMSE by 85.56% relative to OpenWAM with HandTouch, and real-robot and generalization experiments on unseen objects and scenes show consistent performance gains over existing WAM baselines.

topic_matches.title: MOSU2: Long-range Navigation System with Multi-modal Scene Understanding
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces MOSU2, a long-range navigation system that performs two-stage trajectory selection, where an initial contextual reasoning stage selectively triggers a second stage that retrieves and aligns geometric and dynamic evidence for navigation decisions in complex outdoor scenes. Built on MOSU, MOSU2 integrates GPS-based route following with multi-modal traversability analysis and conditional retrieval of motion and geometry cues to handle interactions with vehicles, cyclists, pedestrians, traffic signals, and temporary restrictions. In real-world outdoor experiments involving stop gestures, construction sites, crosswalks, and shared roads, MOSU2 increases mean navigation success from 61.8% to 94.2% and condition-detection accuracy from 72.2% to 91.4% compared to its single-image predecessor, at roughly 2.2× higher mean decision latency.

topic_matches.title: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
topic_matches.institution: FDU; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Sharpa Robotics; The Chinese University of Hong Kong
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents DexForesight, a framework that trains an action-conditioned spatial world model from offline depth, hand geometry, and demonstration trajectories, then injects its dynamics-aware latent representations into a dexterous policy so that, at deployment, the policy operates using only RGB, language, and robot state without explicit future prediction. The learned world model predicts 3D hand-point motion and visual feature changes, capturing articulated hand dynamics and scene changes, including motions of fingers occluded from the cameras, and these predictive queries are aligned with policy queries to condition action generation. On 11 DexJoCo simulation tasks, DexForesight raises the base policy’s overall success rate from 49.4% to 60.5%, and on three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks it achieves 58.3% success versus 50.0% for the strongest baseline.

topic_matches.title: Beyond Memory Limits: A Hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Map Representation for Large-Scale 3D Autonomous Exploration
topic_matches.overview: The paper proposes FLAVOR, a hierarchical spatio-temporal mapping framework for UAV exploration that restricts dense metric geometry to a robot-centric local map while storing global information as compact LiDAR-keyframe visibility records, pending frontier tasks, and a sparse topological graph anchored to odometry. FLAVOR reconstructs frontiers and viewpoints from stored observations and instantiates topological routes against the current local map when returning to task regions, enabling long-horizon exploration without growing the dense map. In simulation, FLAVOR achieves 31.98–41.88% shorter exploration time and a 94–99% smaller map memory footprint than the best baseline that completes all three scenes, and in real-world forest and construction-site deployments it reduces map memory footprint by 92.67% and 62.42%, respectively, relative to an explicit point-cloud ikd-tree while preserving task continuity.

topic_matches.title: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
topic_matches.institution: BJUT; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; JD Explore Academy; University of Cambridge
topic_matches.overview: The paper introduces Kinematic Action Models (KAMs), which treat whole-body motion generation as the core action backbone and use a pretrained humanoid motion generator, Kimodo, combined with lightweight ControlNet-based visual conditioning and a root–body–hand hierarchy for humanoid loco-manipulation. Kimodo-Policy, an instantiation of KAMs with motion-history conditioning and repeated action-chunk prediction, is pretrained on large-scale loco-manipulation data and then task-conditioned using visual observations and execution feedback for closed-loop control. On HumanoidArena, Kimodo-Policy attains 72.14% overall success, achieves competitive performance on SIMPLE, and reaches 60% mean success across eight real-world tasks using 678M parameters (92M trainable), with ablations indicating that the pretrained motion backbone is a key contributor to performance.

topic_matches.title: Design of a hybrid tendon-linkage finger with coupled and adaptive motion
topic_matches.institution: Korea Institute of Machinery & Materials (KIMM); University of Science & Technology (UST)
topic_matches.overview: The paper presents a hybrid tendon–linkage robotic finger with four mechanical DOFs driven by three actuators, where MCP abduction/adduction is driven via a bevel gear, MCP and PIP flexion/extension are actuated by separate bidirectional tendons, and the DIP joint is passively coupled to the PIP joint through a four-bar linkage with a torsional spring and stopper. Tendon routing introduces mechanical coupling between MCP and PIP joints, and kinematic analysis plus ArUco-based experiments show that the realized coupled joint motion closely matches theoretical predictions, though adaptive motion is partially constrained by interference between linkage components. Experiments with cylindrical, cuboid, and irregular objects demonstrate contact-dependent adaptation and varied grasp postures without an independently actuated DIP joint, achieving a mean peak fingertip force of 4.56 N.
